2. The browser tab inventory successfully lists the existing `music.163.com` tab.
3. The agent attempts to bind the listed tab using `cua.getTab(...)`.
4. Browser control rejects the action before page inspection or song collection.

> Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The site-safety policy blocks this action; no user permission prompt or Auto-review was attempted. Browser use is not permitted on https://music.163.com. This report does not assume the block is a confirmed bug and does not request disabling or bypassing security controls. After the denial, the agent did not attempt alternate access to the blocked site. No credentials, cookies, account identifiers, screenshots, or conversation logs are included.

items.body:
### What happens

Every `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` authenticated with a "Sign in with ChatGPT" token-sharing access token (scope `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct`) returns Cloudflare's `520: Web server is returning an unknown error` within about 0.1 s when the connection uses IPv4. The identical request over IPv6 returns 200.

An unauthenticated request over IPv4 gets a normal 401 from the origin, so the IPv4 path reaches the origin. Only requests authenticated with the ChatGPT token fail.

I hit this through OpenCode v2.0.28, which uses this route for ChatGPT sign-in, and reproduced it with curl outside OpenCode. First failure: 2026-10-14 01:29 UTC. The last successful request before that was 2026-10-13 02:35 UTC. status.openai.com shows no incident.

### Reproduction

Same token and body each time, pinned to each address, at 2026-10-14 05:51:55 UTC:

```sh
curl --resolve 'api.openai.com:443:<address>' -X POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-6-astra","service_tier":"priority","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Reply with exactly the word: pong"}]}],"stream":true,"store":false}'
```

| Address | Auth | Status | cf-ray |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 162.159.140.245 | token | 520 | a4a450a2baec8186-EWR |
| 172.66.0.243 | token | 520 | a4a450a37cf68815-EWR |
| 162.159.140.245 | token | 520 | a4a450a48df428c2-IAD |
| 172.66.0.243 | token | 520 | a4a450a589412c1f-IAD |
| 2606:4700:7::f3 | token | 200 | a4a450a698059c6d-IAD |
| 2a06:98c1:58::f3 | token | 200 | a4a450b0d8f9dd0c-IAD |
| 162.159.140.245 | none | 401 | a4a450ba9fbd58d7-EWR |

### Ruled out

- **Model:** gpt-5.5, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol all fail the same way.
- **Request body:** with or without `service_tier: "priority"`, and plain JSON or zstd-compressed, all fail.
- **Token freshness:** it still fails right after a token refresh.
- **Cloudflare colo:** IPv4 fails through both EWR and IAD.

### Unknown

I can't tell whether every IPv4 client is affected or only my address, because I tested from one network. I can share the client IP privately.

### Workaround

Forcing IPv6 for api.openai.com makes every request succeed.

items.title: Desktop: Streamable HTTP MCP refresh fans out across 55 retained task contexts, causing a 1,790-request burst

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop app `26.911.61220` (bundle build `9647`), bundled backend `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.2.6`.
The app version was read from its installed bundle metadata and the backend version from the bundled executable. Incident task metadata predominantly records `0.155.0-alpha.2.6`; some retained contexts were created under an earlier backend version.

### What subscription do you have?

Using a custom enterprise model provider. The ChatGPT subscription tier was not collected for this investigation.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS `26.3.1`, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A runtime-wide startup/reinitialization wave started all 12 globally configured Streamable HTTP MCP integrations across 55 retained task contexts in approximately three seconds. It produced a large authenticated request burst against a remote MCP gateway, including integrations that the model was not using, and was followed by widespread startup failures. The cohort included 48 subagents and 7 parent tasks; 47 of the 55 contexts were created before the incident day.

The report concerns the multiplication across retained contexts and concurrent discovery load. Initial discovery of enabled servers is expected; simply configuring 12 servers is not being reported as invalid behavior.

**Observed on October 13, 2026, UTC:**

- `19:43:58.407–19:44:01.400`: the desktop log records **660 startup events**, exactly **12 remote integrations × 55 distinct task IDs**.
- `19:43:59.361–19:44:47.338`: the gateway records **1,790 authenticated incoming POST requests** for the affected user, approximately 48 seconds. The one-hour query contained 1,850 request records total and did not hit its 2,000-record limit.
- The desktop log records **438 failed startup events** for those integrations, including HTTP 503 during OAuth metadata discovery and transport requests. A separately hosted MCP service also returned HTTP 429 during the same wave.
- 516 logged `ListToolsRequest` processing events match the affected user's request intervals. No `CallToolRequest` events matched those intervals; the local model rollout records inspected for the burst contain shell operations rather than model-issued MCP business-tool calls.

The incoming request count excludes anonymous OAuth metadata/challenge traffic and upstream requests made by the gateway, so it is not a count of all network traffic. Startup event counts are reported as event counts, not as a count of simultaneously established sockets.

A redacted example for one integration, from the desktop log (task IDs and server names replaced):

```text
2026-10-13T19:43:58.407Z mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=remote-pack-01 status=starting threadId=retained-task-01
2026-10-13T19:43:58.482Z mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=remote-pack-01 status=starting threadId=retained-task-02
2026-10-13T19:43:58.559Z mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=remote-pack-01 status=starting threadId=retained-task-03
```

Representative errors, with identifiers/URLs removed:

```text
MCP startup failed: failed to resolve OAuth metadata before using stored credentials
Metadata error: OAuth metadata discovery failed for [redacted MCP URL]
Caused by: unexpected HTTP status 503 Service Unavailable

MCP startup failed: Transport send error ... unexpected server response: HTTP 503: no available server

HTTP 429: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Too many requests. Please retry later."}}
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a measured incident with a source-level investigation, **not yet a deterministic reproduction**. We deliberately did not replay a global refresh against production endpoints.

The relevant setup is:

1. Configure 12 distinct remote MCP endpoints globally in `~/.codex/config.toml`, with normal Streamable HTTP/OAuth settings.
2. Use a long-lived desktop app session with multiple parent tasks and subagents, leaving task contexts retained.
3. A runtime-wide refresh/reinitialization occurs. The precise UI/background event that initiated the observed wave is unknown.
4. Observe all integrations entering startup across many retained contexts within seconds, even when those integrations are not being used for business tool calls.

**Configuration checks already performed:**

- Both the incident-time TOML backup and the current TOML parse successfully.
- Each of the 12 endpoint URLs appears once in the incident configuration; no duplicate endpoint registrations were found there.
- The integrations are ordinary global `[mcp_servers.<id>]` entries with `url`, optional `scopes`, and pre-registered OAuth client/callback settings. Global scope intentionally makes them available across tasks.
- No custom `[agents]` concurrency limits, profile-based MCP overrides, startup script loop, HTTP header helper, or user-configured MCP retry loop was present. Project entries in the user config only set trust levels; no ancestor project-level `.codex/config.toml` files were found for the affected task working directories.
- The relevant integration plugin is skills-only and does not register a second set of those MCP endpoints.
- No documented setting was identified that both keeps these servers available and bounds this cross-task refresh behavior. Per-server startup timeouts and tool allowlists are not equivalent to preventing connection initialization.

For an isolated maintainer reproduction, instrument local test MCP endpoints to count initialization, notification, and tool-list requests; create/retain multiple root and subagent contexts, then exercise the global refresh and shared-auth-change paths. This proposed experiment was not run during the investigation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Enabled servers may require discovery, but a configuration/auth refresh should not generate a large simultaneous startup wave proportional to every retained task context without appropriate limits.

Please consider:

- Avoid prewarming unused/parked contexts merely because a global refresh was requested.
- Preserve deferred startup for eligible subagents across refreshes where safe.
- Bound discovery concurrency across the app-server, not only within each session.
- Coalesce equivalent catalog/initialization work while preserving configuration, authorization, and task-isolation boundaries.
- Refresh only the affected connection when appropriate instead of forcing unrelated integrations to reconnect.

A supported configuration workaround would also be useful if one exists for this installed version.

### Additional information

**Matching-version source observations** (`rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6`, the tag matching the installed backend):

1. [`reload_mcp_config` visits all loaded task IDs and calls each task's refresh](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/app-server/src/mcp_refresh.rs#L10-L50).
2. [`Session::refresh_mcp_config` marks its runtime dirty and schedules background prewarming](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2028-L2066).
3. [Each session's prewarm worker reacts to refresh requests and shared auth changes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp_prewarm.rs#L14-L51). Its request coalescing is per session.
4. [Subagents select `LazyWhenCached`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp_runtime.rs#L381-L386), but [connection setup allows deferred startup only when a previous connection set is available](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs#L252-L256). The source explicitly comments that explicit reconnects replace clients eagerly.
5. [Runtime reconnect handling can omit the previous connection set](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/runtime.rs#L280-L298), and [non-deferred startup work is spawned into each runtime's join set](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.0-alpha.2.6/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs#L743-L766).

These are candidate paths consistent with the measurements, not proof of which initiating event occurred. The global reload/prewarm path and the explicit reconnect path should not be assumed to be the same path without further tracing.

This report focuses on the client's 660 startup events across 55 task contexts. The complete server-side cause of the observed HTTP 503 responses has not been isolated.

As an immediate mitigation, unused global integrations were removed, reducing the affected gateway inventory from 12 to 2. This reduces exposure and does not demonstrate that the lifecycle behavior is fixed. No unknown feature flags, custom builds, or timeout increases were applied.

Related existing reports: #20883 (per-session MCP ownership/pooling) and #21984 (eager per-session startup). This report focuses on the synchronized **Streamable HTTP request burst and remote availability/rate-limit impact**, with matching-version refresh code and correlated client/server measurements. If it belongs under one of those reports, please consolidate it there.

All investigation was through local files, source inspection, and read-only cloud-log queries. No MCP status APIs, tools, or deliberate MCP refresh/reproduction calls were used. Private endpoints, account identifiers, task IDs, credentials, and raw session/server logs are intentionally omitted.

items.body:
### Summary
Codex Desktop for Windows intermittently cancels its own automatic Git review/turn-diff snapshot and logs `Git snapshot became stale`. This occurs when a user sends a normal chat message, without asking for a Git operation. After staging the previously untracked files, the affected Git commands are fast when run independently, but the desktop still cancels them in some turns.

### Environment
- Windows desktop app MSIX: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64`
- Git: `2.53.0.windows.3` (bundled runtime Git)
- Local, valid Git repository on an `E:` drive
- Private workspace path, account name and repository identity intentionally omitted

### Steps and observations
1. Open an existing local Git repository in Codex Desktop and send a short chat message.
2. The desktop automatically starts `turn-diff-capture-start` (`source=turn_diff_analytics`), with Git commands against a temporary index.
3. Intermittently, the desktop cancels its own Git command (`failureReason=canceled`, `aborted=true`, `exitCode=null`, `timedOut=false`) and logs `Git snapshot became stale`.
4. Restarting the desktop did not prevent recurrence. Staging approximately 1,893 previously untracked files reduced an independent snapshot probe from ~50 seconds to <1 second, but the desktop still produced the error after staging. A test of `git-review-mode = "last-turn-only"` followed by a restart did not prevent it either; that setting was reverted.

Redacted log examples:
```text
2026-10-14T02:02:15.443Z [git] write-tree
  requestKind=turn-diff-capture-start source=turn_diff_analytics
  durationMs=527 aborted=true failureReason=canceled
  exitCode=null timedOut=false success=false
2026-10-14T02:02:16.245Z Failed to start turn diff analytics capture
  errorMessage="Git snapshot became stale"

2026-10-14T05:23:33.588Z [git] add
  requestKind=turn-diff-capture-start source=turn_diff_analytics
  durationMs=0 aborted=true failureReason=canceled
  exitCode=null timedOut=false success=false
2026-10-14T05:23:33.598Z Failed to start turn diff analytics capture
  errorMessage="Git snapshot became stale"
```

The equivalent local temporary-index probe succeeded: `git add -u` took ~0.06 s, `git write-tree` ~0.05 s, and the whole probe ~0.36 s; the real Git index was unchanged. `git status`, connectivity check and remote fetch/push also worked. Some desktop captures succeeded, so the failure is intermittent. The exact invalidation trigger is not yet established.

### Expected behavior
Routine turns should not produce an error from automatic Git change capture. If a snapshot becomes obsolete, the app should cancel/retry it quietly without presenting it as a user-facing Git failure, while preserving normal review behavior.

### Related reports
- #50920 describes canceled turn-diff captures on Windows, with a separate large temporary-pack accumulation effect.
- #30820 describes eager review snapshot work and resource spikes.

I can provide a small sanitized log excerpt or run a focused diagnostic build if maintainers need more information.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.71326

### What subscription do you have?

Not disclosed in this public report.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux desktop. `uname -mprs`: `Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 unknown`.

### What issue are you seeing?

I observed a difference between a fresh local task created by my dot and a fresh Codex CLI session on the same computer: the dot-created task reported that my global `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` policy was absent from its supplied startup context, while the CLI session received that policy automatically.

I checked this with a new, read-only dot-created task in a task directory outside my normal workspace. The delegation prompt did not include the policy contents. Before any tool use or file reads, the task reported that the global policy and two named sections were absent. I then instructed it to read the global file and the relevant service runbook explicitly. Those reads succeeded, and it successfully verified my GitHub identity using the documented existing authentication route.

For comparison, a fresh CLI session outside the normal workspace quoted the two sections without tool calls or file reads. I also checked that session's local startup record and confirmed that the supplied user-instruction message contained both sections. The CLI comparison used version 0.162.1.

The practical impact was a wrong GitHub authentication diagnosis in an earlier task: it used a different CLI authentication route, encountered an invalid session, and asked me to reauthenticate even though the documented existing route worked. Explicitly reading the local guidance corrected that diagnosis without changing credentials.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are the observed workflow and a suggested minimal comparison, not a claim that this reproduces on every account:

1. Have a readable global `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` with two short, distinctive, non-sensitive instructions. Do not include those instructions in the test prompts.
2. Ask a dot to create a fresh local task on the connected Linux computer, without copying earlier conversation history, in a task directory outside the normal project workspace.
3. Ask the task, before any tool use or file reads, whether its supplied startup context contains the global policy and the two named instructions. Require it to report absence rather than infer their contents.
4. After that initial report, ask it to read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` explicitly and compare the file with what it reported receiving automatically.
5. Start a fresh CLI session on the same computer, also outside the normal project workspace. Ask the same pre-tool-use question without supplying the policy contents. Inspect the CLI startup record locally to distinguish automatic inclusion from later file reads.

Observed result: the dot-created task reported absence before tools, then read the file successfully; the CLI quoted the sections without tools, and its startup record confirmed inclusion.

### What is the expected behavior?

I expect supported global instruction loading to be consistent for local tasks, including tasks created by dots, with the documented precedence rules. If dot-created tasks intentionally use different instruction-loading behavior, please document that difference and provide a visible indication of which instruction sources were loaded.

The public AGENTS.md documentation describes global instruction discovery before work: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md

### Additional information

- In this setup, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to a readable shared policy file. The final file is 11,864 bytes. The same file worked in the CLI comparison. Symlink handling has not been isolated as a cause.
- Host-side checks found no global `AGENTS.override.md` and no `CODEX_HOME` override in the inspected tool environment. I have not established the launcher's effective configuration independently.
- The dot-side evidence is the task's explicit report before tool use, followed by successful file reads. I have not independently captured the dot backend's assembled startup prompt. Please treat this as an observed discrepancy requiring investigation, not a proven loader root cause.
- Workaround: explicitly require each delegated task to read the global policy and relevant runbooks before substantive work. Successful explicit reading does not demonstrate automatic loading.
- Related: #27705 reports missing global instructions in ordinary project chats; #37950 concerns voice versus text instruction delivery. This report adds the fresh dot-created local task versus CLI comparison. Please consolidate if it belongs with an existing issue.
- I am not attributing this to an update or requesting changes to permission safeguards. This report is about instruction delivery, separate from Full Access/default-permission requests.

items.title: Refresh model instructions in incremental-tool context windows
items.body:
Refresh model instructions in incremental-tool context windows

## Why

Incremental-tool windows recorded base instructions only at setup, so a catalog refresh for the same model could leave active instructions stale. Instruction changes need to reach the model without rewriting the existing history prefix.

## What changed

- Track model identity and instruction content independently, appending a `model_instructions` developer message when either changes. Explicitly mark replacement or removal of base instructions, and avoid repeating unchanged updates.
- Start new windows after compaction with the latest model instructions while preserving custom base instructions.
- Preserve the recorded window base during local compaction retries, including empty instructions, and rebuild current model instructions when reconstructing child context.

## Testing

Add integration tests and request snapshots for catalog refreshes, instruction removal, model switches, compaction, restart, and forks. Extend regression coverage for legacy snapshots and local compaction retries.

### What issue are you seeing?

ChatGPT for Android crashes while opening, scrolling, or returning to the Codex remote chat list. ADB crash logs repeatedly show an uncaught main-thread exception:

```text
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
Process: com.openai.chatgpt
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Key "remote-thread-list-date-x2x0" was already used. If you are using LazyColumn/Row please make sure you provide a unique key for each item.
```

The stack includes `androidx.compose.ui.node.LayoutNode` and `androidx.compose.ui.platform.AndroidComposeView` rendering calls. App frames are obfuscated.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected account/device:
1. Open ChatGPT for Android.
2. Enter Codex and load the remote chat list.
3. Scroll the list. The app crashes.
4. Reopen the app. It can sometimes display the list while left untouched.
5. Opening a chat via Search chats succeeds, but returning to the main list can trigger the same crash.

The visible list has Today, Previous 7 Days, Previous 30 Days, and September date headings. The exact thread ordering/data condition that creates the duplicate key has not been isolated.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Codex chat list should load, scroll, and allow navigation into and out of chats without terminating the Android app.

### Additional information

Observed on October 14, 2026:
- Phone: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, model SM-S928U.
- Android: release 17, API level 37, as reported by ADB.
- Package: com.openai.chatgpt.
- Installed app version: 1.2026.279; versionCode 2627911.
- Google Play shows ChatGPT (Beta) and beta enrollment; no Update button was offered when checked.
- Remote host: Windows 10, x64.

Evidence and attempts:
- An initial retained crash buffer contained 14 matching exceptions. Some precede the current installation timestamp, so their app version is unverified.
- After a force-stop/relaunch of the currently installed version, three more matching crashes appeared at device-reported times 01:21:07.982, 01:21:17.770, and 01:21:33.727 on 10-14. Device log timestamps have not been converted to another timezone.

The immediate failure is duplicate lazy-list keys. The key name suggests a remote-thread date heading, but the specific grouping/ordering cause requires developer investigation and deobfuscation.

Please investigate unique keys for date headings across the complete rendered remote thread list and provide a fixed Android build or supported mitigation. This is an Android mobile UI report, not a CLI crash.

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS ARM64, Codex CLI authenticated via ChatGPT can run text turns, but the built-in image-generation extension is not exposed in newly created app-server threads. A direct `codex exec` image-generation attempt on the previous CLI build reached the image backend and returned HTTP 403. After upgrading to the current CLI, image-gen tool registration remains unavailable even with the stable feature enabled.

## Environment

- macOS ARM64
- Codex CLI `0.162.1` (upgraded from `0.145.0`)
- ChatGPT OAuth login succeeds; access token is current
- Account can generate images in ChatGPT web
- Model: `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-luna`, both text turns run successfully
- `image_generation = true` in `~/.codex/config.toml`
- Also tested with `imagegenext = true`; no change
- No `OPENAI_API_KEY` involved

## Reproduction

1. Start a fresh app-server process using `codex app-server --stdio --enable image_generation`.
2. Initialize over JSONL; start an ephemeral thread with `serviceName: "chatgpt_cca"`, model `gpt-5.6-terra`, and workspace-write sandbox.
3. Ask for one simple image using the built-in image-generation capability.
4. The model reports the tool is absent. Another direct Codex CLI test reports `TypeError: tools.image_gen is not a function`; the direct official app-server test reports `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'imagegen')`.
5. Repeated after `codex features enable imagegenext`, with no change.

On the previous CLI build, an actual image request reached the image endpoint and returned `403 Forbidden` with body `{"detail":"Forbidden"}`.

## Additional diagnostic observation

The same account's ChatGPT web image generation succeeds. In the app-server's `account/rateLimits/updated` notification, `planType` is reported as `free` even though ChatGPT OAuth is used and web image generation works. This may indicate an account entitlement/plan mapping issue; please confirm whether this is expected for ChatGPT-connected Codex CLI accounts.

## Expected

The built-in image-generation extension/tool is registered and callable for an eligible ChatGPT-authenticated account, or the app-server returns a specific entitlement reason instead of omitting the tool. If this CLI surface is not entitled, please clarify the supported client / plan requirements.

No credentials, tokens, local paths, or user data are included in this report.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

ChatGPT desktop Linux package `chatgpt 26.1007.71326`, verified through dpkg (not the About dialog). The app-bundled Codex runtime is `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 unknown`

- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, GNOME 50.1, Wayland desktop session; normal app launch without diagnostic flags. The app's actual display backend was not independently established in this investigation.
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, driver `595.99.02`. Loaded kernel module, installed module and nvidia-smi agree.
- 128 GB installed RAM (approximately 125 GiB usable).
- Official OpenAI Debian package/repository.

### What issue are you seeing?

ChatGPT intermittently stops accepting interaction and Ubuntu displays its Wait / Force Quit dialog. It can feel as though the machine has frozen; I have not yet established whether other desktop apps remain interactive during these pauses.

Before reinstalling ChatGPT, choosing Wait did not restore the app, leaving it unusable. Since reinstalling, choosing Wait allows the app to resume, but intermittent stalls remain. The reinstall improved recovery; it did not eliminate the issue. The exact reason for the improvement is unknown.

A read-only, AI-assisted investigation found a correlated incident on October 14, 2026 at 03:38 UTC (October 13 at 11:38 p.m. EDT). The accessibility service identified the running ChatGPT process as unresponsive, and the app reported renderer unavailability at the same second.

Sanitized excerpts; app timestamps are UTC, journal timestamps below are converted from EDT:

```text
2026-10-14 03:38:32Z at-spi2-registryd: Disabling unresponsive app with pid [ChatGPT PID]
2026-10-14T03:38:32.390Z warning [dynamic-app-tools-native-pipe] dynamic_app_tools_request_failed errorMessage="The Codex app renderer is unavailable" method=tools/list
2026-10-14T03:38:32.407Z warning [electron-message-handler] mcp_extension_tool_discovery_failed error="MCP startup failed: timed out awaiting tools/list after 10s" server=codex_app
2026-10-14 03:38:52Z at-spi2-registryd: Re-enabling app with pid [ChatGPT PID]
```

Background services and some app logging continued during this interval. The 20 seconds measure accessibility disable/re-enable, not necessarily the entire visible freeze. The tool timeout could be a consequence of the stall rather than its cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Intermittent observed behavior; no deterministic minimal reproducer is available:

1. Launch ChatGPT normally on the Linux desktop and use the app.
2. Occasionally, clicking/interacting stops working and Ubuntu offers Wait or Force Quit.
3. Choose Wait. With the current installation the app eventually resumes; before reinstalling it did not recover.

The exact action triggering the logged incident is unknown. Please suggest a supported, narrowly scoped renderer/event-loop diagnostic to capture during the next occurrence.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should remain responsive to input during normal use and internal tool discovery, without triggering the desktop's unresponsive-application dialog.

### Additional information

- Package verification (`dpkg -V chatgpt`) found no changed packaged files. A successful repository refresh on October 13 found no newer ChatGPT package.
- Historical system sampling around the incident showed approximately 114.5 GiB available RAM, zero swapping and 86% CPU idle over the surrounding ten-minute interval. The system NVMe averaged 0.29 ms I/O wait. A separate external disk was busy; no causal link to the stall was established. Coarse sampling cannot exclude brief spikes.
- Checked kernel logs showed no corresponding OOM kill, NVIDIA Xid, driver/library mismatch, kernel lockup or NVMe I/O error. A previous driver/library mismatch had already been resolved by reboot before this incident.
- Earlier tests on October 7 with an older app build (`26.1002.52244`) did not resolve the previous persistent freeze: `--disable-gpu`, `--ozone-platform=wayland`, and an empty temporary app profile. These were not controlled retests of the current build. The October 9 reinstall preserved the normal user profile.
- The current app log also recorded 2,402 `thread/read` failures with `thread access denied` over roughly 92 minutes. These occurred outside the freeze interval too, so their relevance is uncertain.
- GNOME logged one `Cursor update failed: drmModeAtomicCommit: Invalid argument` about five minutes after this incident; a connection is unproven.

Related reports reviewed: #47628 (Linux typing freezes with ResizeObserver bursts), #43481 (text insertion/dictation freeze), and #53106 (Windows/WSL renderer-readiness/tool-discovery timeout). None establishes the same trigger or cause here; please consolidate if appropriate.

Only selected diagnostic excerpts are included. No raw logs, chat content, account identifiers, private file paths, credentials or session transcripts are attached.

### App version and platform

- **Affected version:** ChatGPT / Codex macOS desktop `26.1007.30912` (build 20156).
- **Working comparison:** `26.930.31730` (build 12947), restored via rollback.
- **Platform:** macOS on Apple Silicon.

### Issue

The **Background Processes** section previously appeared in the **right-hand conversation details sidebar**, listing long-running commands started by Codex. For example, when Codex launched a Go service with `go run main.go start`, I could see the corresponding command/session under **Background Processes**, beneath the project/changes area.

After upgrading to `26.1007.30912`, that section/entry no longer appeared in the right-hand details sidebar for agent-started commands. After rolling back to `26.930.31730`, the section was visible again.

This is **not** about:
- The separate integrated **Terminal** panel/tab.
- Command output embedded in the main conversation.
- Whether the Go program itself starts or runs successfully.

The issue is specifically the **visibility and discoverability of agent-started background processes in the right-hand details sidebar**.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local project conversation in the ChatGPT / Codex macOS desktop app.
2. Ask Codex to start a long-running process, such as a Go development server with `go run main.go`.
3. Open the conversation's **right-hand details sidebar**.
4. Look for the **Background Processes** section and the command that Codex started.
5. Compare the behavior between `26.930.31730` and `26.1007.30912`.

**Observed:** The older version shows the background-process entry in the sidebar; the newer version did not show it in the user's test.

**Expected:** Agent-started background processes remain visible and accessible in the details sidebar, or the app provides a clearly documented replacement location.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Was the **Background Processes** section intentionally removed or moved in recent macOS desktop releases?
2. If it moved, where can users view and manage commands/processes started by Codex?
3. If this is a regression, which version is expected to restore it?

The exact first affected release and underlying cause are **not yet established**. This report describes the observed before/after UI behavior, not a confirmed implementation change.

### Related, separately reported issues

Two *different* features also disappeared in the 26.1007 series, but they already have their own issues and **are not being requested here**:

- #53042 — standalone Quick Chat window/launcher.
- #52483 — selected-text **More details** action.

This issue is **only** about the right-sidebar **Background Processes** list.

items.title: [Windows][26.1007.21434 build 13901] Remote chat opening repeatedly crashes renderer: chrome.dll +0x4DA250D, null read 0xC0000005

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### Component and environment

Windows desktop app (installed as OpenAI.Codex), observed 14 October 2026:
- MSIX package: 26.1007.2314.0.
- Internal app: 26.1007.21434, build 13901.
- x86_64; Windows 11.
- Bundled faulting module: chrome.dll 155.0.8059.40.
- Workflow: one Windows PC displays Codex chats executing on a second connected Windows PC; Android Remote and the dot are also used.
- Wispr Flow 1.6.1144 is installed/running. No new user instruction was submitted to the target chat during the two controlled reproduction tests. Background activity on every paired device was not isolated.

### Reproduction and impact

1. Open an existing Codex chat executing on the connected Windows host.
2. In two controlled openings, the controller's primary renderer crashed roughly 6–8 seconds after the navigation request.
3. The entire primary window goes black, then reloads. The main desktop process and host execution continue.
4. The user reports slow chat recovery and significantly reduced Priority/Today activity lists after recovery. In a prior incident, dictated text landed in a new chat/composer after the reload.

Both controlled openings used the intended remote-control host, verified from request/route logs. This is a reproduction with one affected chat, not a universal claim that every remote chat crashes. A separate proposed remote-chat comparison was invalid because its navigation selected the local host; that interval is excluded as a control.

### Matching native crash signature

A temporary read-only watcher preserved two native Crashpad minidumps locally before automatic cleanup. Both are renderer crashes and identify the sampled primary-renderer process.

| Field | Capture 1 | Capture 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Crash time, 14 Oct, AWST (UTC+8) | 11:09:49.886 | 11:21:22.061 |
| Exception | 0xC0000005 | 0xC0000005 |
| Access | Read from 0x0 | Read from 0x0 |
| Module | chrome.dll | chrome.dll |
| Module version | 155.0.8059.40 | 155.0.8059.40 |
| Fault offset | 0x4DA250D | 0x4DA250D |
| Debug file | chrome.dll.pdb | chrome.dll.pdb |
| PDB symbol identifier | 6994A0558347FDEA4C4C44205044422E1 | 6994A0558347FDEA4C4C44205044422E1 |

The exception-context RIP matches the exception address in both captures. The native exception is an invalid memory read; no V8 OOM/fatal diagnostic annotation was found. This does not rule out every possible memory-pressure contribution.

At the first controlled crash, the last sample of the affected renderer was approximately 1,237 MiB private memory. Private memory is not JavaScript heap usage; this is not proof of a leak or OOM.

Both captures recorded native/web accessibility mode flags, including inline text boxes and extended properties. Accessibility/Wispr involvement has not been isolated and is a lead only. Raw stack address candidates are not presented as an unwound stack.

### Host and request evidence

- Before the earlier user-reported 10:46:55 crash, remote thread/read, thread/resume, thread/turns/list and three thread/items/list responses succeeded. The last items response was approximately 0.5 seconds before the retained crash timestamp.
- A read-only check of the execution host for 10:44–10:49 AWST found no retained app/server crash, restart, disconnect, rejection or stream-collision warning. Its app/server processes retained their 11 October start times.
- The affected chat was already paginated; its host rollout was approximately 41.25 MiB. This does not measure controller payload sizes or loaded memory.
- The controller main desktop process retained its 09:52:22 start time across the two controlled crashes.
- Other intervals contain queue-full/expiry, sequence-gap and missing-active-turn-ID errors. Those are separate evidence and are not asserted as the cause of these native crashes.

### What has been tried

- PC/app restarts did not eliminate the user's recurring symptoms.
- Both matching native crashes occurred with --disable-gpu confirmed active. Software graphics is not a sufficient fix for this signature.
- A small local chat stayed open during an approximately 50-second control observation.
- An earlier opening of a large locally executing chat also produced a renderer-crash sidecar, without a matching native dump. Remote control is not established as the sole cause of the overall problem.
- Installed-code inspection found a volatile activity-view snapshot and temporary held-unread state, initialized from available metadata with a visible-item limit of 10. An offline test using synthetic metadata demonstrated a reduced snapshot after recovery without deleting canonical records. It does not verify preservation of every actual user activity item or reproduce the live UI/watcher.
- No profile/history deletion, pairing reset, signed-bundle modification, or forced termination of active work was performed in these controlled tests. Pending text and relevant dictation history were preserved privately.

### Engineering request

Please:
1. Symbolicate chrome.dll +0x4DA250D for this exact build and investigate the repeated null-read signature during remote chat display/history/state updates.
2. Check native accessibility/rendering interactions as well as history/live-state handling; no specific cause is claimed yet.
3. Provide a private supported channel for the two native dumps and matching diagnostic metadata, or matching public debug symbols. The official Electron symbol server returned HTTP 404 for this PDB identifier.
4. Identify a fixed desktop build or supported mitigation preserving chats, pending input and running work.
5. Investigate reconstruction of Priority/Today activity lists after renderer recovery.

Related symptom reports: #51313 and #53192. Their root causes have not been established as identical.

Submitted with the affected user's explicit authorization. Private chat titles/IDs, business content, account/device identifiers, local usernames/paths, raw logs, personal drafts and native dump files are excluded from this public report.

### Offline analysis update — 14 October 2026

Additional local, read-only analysis of the same two retained captures narrows the failure:

- Windows 11 Home, OS build 26300, x64.
- The installed DLL's PDB identifier matches both captures. Captured instruction bytes match the installed DLL.
- The fault is `48 39 10`: `cmp qword ptr [rax], rdx`, at `chrome.dll +0x4DA250D`. `RAX=0` in both exception contexts.
- Immediately preceding code loads a 32-bit field, sign-extends it, shifts left three bits, and masks it with a heap base. That field is zero in both captures. This matches Chromium's compressed-pointer decoding pattern; the owner/class is not established by this observation alone.
- A read-only x64 PE unwinder recovered the same first 12 frame offsets in both captures. All 11 intervening direct call sites were independently checked against the DLL and target the preceding frame's containing function. Synthetic allocation/register/frame-pointer/prolog checks also passed. This is PE-unwind-derived evidence, not PDB symbolication.
- Relevant caller functions reference static strings for `LocalFrameView::performLayout`, `LocalFrameView::layout`, `LocalFrameView::UpdateStyleAndLayout`, and `Document::UpdateStyleAndLayout`.
- The later native getter callback at `+0x3002B10` appears in a static binding record adjacent to `scrollLeft`, between the `scrollTop` and `scrollWidth` records. This points to a JavaScript scroll-position read forcing layout; the JavaScript caller and DOM node are not identified.

First twelve corroborated frames, all relative to chrome.dll:

```text
04DA250D
04D60016
04DA25B6
04D60016
04DA25B6
04D60016
005C41E9
005C097F
0547F97D
0547B2D1
0547956D
02FF153D
```

**Source-based inference for engineering review:** the faulting function's child-fragment loop closely matches [Blink SimplifiedLayoutAlgorithm::Layout](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/third_party/blink/renderer/core/layout/simplified_layout_algorithm.cc): it skips out-of-flow fragments, checks list markers/line boxes, and recursively performs simplified layout on other children. The compared static vtable includes a short method returning `LayoutOutsideListMarker`. [PhysicalFragment](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/third_party/blink/renderer/core/layout/physical_fragment.h) documents that a fragment can outlive its layout object and that the object pointer is cleared on destruction.

This strengthens the cached-fragment/layout-object lifetime or invalidation hypothesis. The named function is inferred from control flow/static strings and current upstream source, **not confirmed by symbols for this exact build**. It does not establish why the object pointer is missing, which application update created the state, or whether Wispr/accessibility contributes. Please verify the named path and consider whether invalid cached fragments should reject simplified layout and fall back to full layout before dereferencing their layout objects.

Two further renderer-crash sidecars were recorded at **12:13:32.409 and 12:13:45.262 AWST** while this investigation was performing offline analysis. No navigation was initiated by the investigation during that interval. Those native dumps were not retained, so the later failures are **not claimed to share this exact exception signature**.

The duplicate suggestions #53343, #53192 and #53180 have similar macOS symptoms/framework versions; #52770 reports Windows reloads while switching running subagents. The reviewed reports do not supply this matching Windows null-read/PDB/RVA signature, so a shared root cause remains unverified.

All raw dumps, heap addresses/content, private chat/account/device identifiers and local paths remain excluded.

### What issue are you seeing?

```text
UnsupportedOperation("windows unelevated restricted-token sandbox cannot enforce split writable root sets directly; refusing to run unsandboxed")
```

Reproduction conditions:

- Built-in **Approve for me** preset; recorded approval policy `on-request` and reviewer `auto_review`. No named/custom permission profile was selected.
- The chat has a local-project working directory and additional allowed temporary/writable directories.
- The working directory is unchanged between the compared manual and scheduled turns.
- In the manual turn, the recorded detailed filesystem policy explicitly grants write access to the working directory. In the scheduled turn, that entry is absent, although additional writable directories remain. This differs from the legacy workspace-write representation, which treats cwd as an implicit writable root.
- The inspected bundled CLI reports `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`. This is not a verified desktop About-version value.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the pattern reproduced on an existing installation, not a verified clean-install minimal reproducer:

1. Open a local-project chat using the conditions above.
2. Run an existing local Python script's read-only status/prepare command manually. It succeeds.
3. Have a heartbeat targeting that same chat run the same command.
4. Observe process-startup failure with the exception above; the command itself never runs.
5. Compare the recorded effective filesystem policies: the manual turn includes a write grant for cwd; the heartbeat does not.
6. Re-save the existing automation and run another test through the actual scheduled-heartbeat path. The same failure recurs. Restore the original daily schedule afterwards.

### What is the expected behavior?

An authorized read-only command should start within a consistent, enforceable sandbox in both paths. A scheduled heartbeat should retain the applicable workspace permissions, subject to managed restrictions. If its configuration cannot be enforced, it should provide an actionable supported recovery path rather than require unrestricted execution.

Related reports: #50120 (named-profile loss during heartbeat scheduling) and #52252 (the same exception in a delegated Windows task). This reproduction uses the built-in preset without a selected named profile and includes an actual command-startup comparison.

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, Codex sessions routed through a local third party compatible gateway intermittently fail or are interrupted. The failures are especially disruptive for long running tasks because a turn can stop before a final response and the user has to recover or resend the request.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Codex desktop
- A local compatible gateway used for model requests
- Date observed: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Shanghai)

## Observed evidence

A request monitor recorded 414 requests after de duplicating by request ID:

- 347 succeeded
- 67 failed
- 34 returned HTTP 503 with `server_is_overloaded` / `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`
- 23 returned upstream 502 errors

The local gateway health and model discovery checks returned HTTP 200 during the same investigation. The observed failures therefore appeared at the upstream capacity or gateway transport layer while the local gateway itself remained reachable.

## Expected behavior

When the upstream provider is at capacity or returns a transient gateway error, Codex should preserve the turn state, report the actual provider and retry status clearly, and allow a safe resume without silently replaying a large request or losing the user's steering message.

## Actual behavior

Long running tasks can be interrupted by capacity or upstream errors. The visible error does not consistently make it clear whether the failure came from the local gateway, the upstream provider, or an automatic retry or replay path. Repeated recovery attempts can create additional load and make it difficult to determine whether a request is still active.

## Reproduction / diagnostics

1. Configure Codex to use a local compatible gateway.
2. Run several ordinary and long running requests.
3. Observe intermittent `503 server_is_overloaded`, `502` upstream failures, or an interrupted turn while the local gateway remains reachable.

I can provide further redacted request IDs and timestamps if maintainers need them.

While Codex computer use is driving another app (in my case the Claude desktop app, Electron, 2.37337.1), every key I type on the physical keyboard is entered twice, in every app. Typing `asdf` in TextEdit produces `aassddff`. A single space arrives as two spaces, which macOS turns into ". " through the double-space period shortcut. The computer is unusable for the person sitting at it until the state clears.

It starts some minutes after Codex begins working in the target app and persists until `SkyComputerUseService` exits. Running `pkill -f SkyComputerUseService` fixes it immediately, with the target app still running (same pid). Quitting the target app also clears it.

Diagnostics while the doubling was active:

- A listen-only `CGEventTap` at `kCGSessionEventTap` saw each physical key exactly once (`eventSourceUnixProcessID` 0, source state 1).
- A listen-only `CGEventTapCreateForPid` tap on TextEdit, placed at `tailAppendEventTap`, also saw each key exactly once, yet TextEdit displayed every character twice. The duplicate therefore enters after event delivery, not through a re-posted `CGEvent`.
- `CGGetEventTapList` showed `SkyComputerUseService` holding three to five active (modifying) per-process keyboard taps (mask `keyDown|keyUp|flagsChanged`), plus a listen-only key tap at the annotated session level. The service binary contains `viewBridgeKeyboardTap`, `keyboardEventTap` and `SystemFocusStealPreventer`, so the background keyboard routing or focus-steal suppression may be inserting the second copy through the text input path.
- Several `SkyComputerUseClient computer-history mcp` processes from earlier sessions (back two days) were still alive, which may be related to #25744.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On macOS 27, let a Codex app thread use computer use to operate the Claude desktop app (Electron) in the background, typing prompts and reading results, over 10 to 30 minutes.
2. Meanwhile, type in any other app (TextEdit, a terminal).
3. After a while, every keystroke is entered twice. `pgrep -fl SkyComputerUseService` shows the service running.
4. `pkill -f SkyComputerUseService`; typing is normal again immediately.

The doubling has not been observed while Codex drives a terminal app (Ghostty).

### What is the expected behavior?

Computer use in a background app should never alter the user's own keyboard input in other apps.

### Additional information

The event-tap lister and key monitor used above are about 30 lines of Swift each; happy to share them.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

windows

### What issue are you seeing?

Title: Why did 34 web-tool actions produce 15.9 million input tokens in a single turn?

I ran one continuous Codex session with five sequential turns, using gpt-6-luna.

Turn 1: Load background information
Web-tool actions: 0
Input tokens: 72,458

Turn 2: Web research
Web-tool actions: 32
Input tokens: 7,216,519

Turn 3: Web research
Web-tool actions: 54
Input tokens: 22,301,794

Turn 4: Web research
Web-tool actions: 34
Input tokens: 15,897,762

Turn 5: Consolidate findings into a final report
Web-tool actions: 0
Input tokens: 648,490

Total reported input tokens: 46,137,023.

These numbers came from thread/tokenUsage/updated. Each turn's usage was calculated by subtracting consecutive end-of-turn cumulative totals, not by repeatedly summing cumulative snapshots.

The counts represent web-tool actions, not unique webpages.

Why did Turn 4 accumulate nearly 16 million input tokens from 34 web-tool actions, while Turn 5, using the existing conversation to produce the final report, required only about 648,000?

Please explain:

1. How much comes from retrieved content versus repeatedly processing existing context?
2. Are unnecessary model/tool round trips amplifying usage, or is there a reporting issue?
3. How do these reported tokens translate into subscription-limit consumption?

The visible search results do not suggest a massive crawl or an enormous volume of retrieved material. Even assuming a few thousand tokens per webpage, that is nowhere near 15.9 million tokens of new content.

So how the hell does a modest web-research task produce this kind of token explosion?

If the explanation is that the same conversation gets counted repeatedly after each tool action, that still raises a serious efficiency and transparency problem. Calling it cumulative usage does not explain why so much repeated processing is necessary, or how much subscription allowance it consumes. A high cache-hit rate alone does not answer these questions either.

Please show the actual breakdown: newly retrieved content, repeated context, model requests, and the resulting quota impact.

Users should not have to reverse-engineer your accounting to understand why a relatively small research task produces tens of millions of reported input tokens.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The affected run used the following workflow:

1. Create a fresh Codex session using gpt-6-luna through the Codex SDK.
2. Turn 1: Provide approximately 102,446 characters of background information.
3. Turns 2–4: Send three successive web-research prompts in the same session. Let the model search and return its findings after each prompt.
4. Turn 5: Ask the model to consolidate the existing findings into a final report without further web searches.
5. Record thread/tokenUsage/updated notifications throughout the session.
6. Calculate each turn's input usage by subtracting the previous turn's final cumulative input total from the current turn's final cumulative input total.

Observed results:

Turn 1: 0 web-tool actions; 72,458 input tokens.
Turn 2: 32 web-tool actions; 7,216,519 input tokens.
Turn 3: 54 web-tool actions; 22,301,794 input tokens.
Turn 4: 34 web-tool actions; 15,897,762 input tokens.
Turn 5: 0 web-tool actions; 648,490 input tokens.

Total: 46,137,023 input tokens.

One context-compaction event was observed during Turn 3.

These are recorded results from one run, not guaranteed identical counts on every reproduction. Web-tool actions are not unique webpage counts. Cumulative snapshots were not repeatedly summed.

### What is the expected behavior?

I expect web research to avoid unnecessary repeated processing and to provide understandable, verifiable usage accounting.

I am not claiming that total input tokens must equal the text retrieved from webpages. However, tens of millions of reported input tokens for this workflow require a concrete explanation.

Please provide a per-request breakdown showing:

1. Newly retrieved content.
2. Existing context processed again.
3. The number of model requests and tool actions.
4. Any additional usage caused by compaction or retries.
5. How this reported usage affects subscription limits.

If unnecessary model/tool round trips are amplifying consumption, please fix them. If these totals are intended accounting, please document why this level of repeated processing is necessary and provide practical controls to reduce it.

A high cache-hit rate alone is not an adequate explanation.

_No response_

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home, Chinese locale, x64, build 26200.
- Microsoft Store desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.
- Window/executable name: ChatGPT / ChatGPT.exe.
- Bundled Codex engine: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Git for Windows: 2.44.0.windows.1.
- A Git-backed development project with hundreds of changed paths relative to an older review baseline.

A subsequent read-only audit established why the path list is large: the review baseline is an October 2 commit, whereas the current HEAD is from October 11. Comparing the baseline to HEAD produces 435 changed entries; the current uncommitted tracked changes relative to HEAD produce 80 entries; the cumulative baseline-to-working-tree diff produces 466 entries. These counts overlap and do not add directly. No paths under common bin/obj/node_modules/dist/build/.vs/target/packages directory names appeared among those tracked changes. This is mostly ordinary source/configuration change history, rather than a huge collection of generated build files. Committing the pending changes alone would not eliminate a diff against the old baseline.

## Desktop reproduction observed on the affected machine

1. Completely exit the desktop app and its child processes, including its bundled codex.exe backend.
2. Launch the desktop app normally with existing projects/history.
3. Select the affected Git-backed project or open its existing conversations. No new user request to run Git is needed.
4. The desktop's automatic changes/review summary starts a command of this shape:

```text
git -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false -c core.quotePath=false
    -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=
    diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --color=never --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/
    <review-baseline-commit> --find-renames --raw --no-abbrev --numstat -z
    -- <hundreds of relative file paths>
```

5. The parent ChatGPT.exe window becomes unresponsive. Captured total command-line length: 32,411 characters. Another desktop run reached 32,469 characters and also froze.

Expected: the changes summary completes, fails with an actionable error, or can be cancelled without blocking the window.

Actual: the window stops responding indefinitely while the native process-creation call is blocked. The child Git process exists in an initialized state, with no execution/CPU progress.

## Native evidence

The main window thread's captured native stack, from the blocking leaf upward, included:

```text
ntdll!NtCreateUserProcess+0x14
KERNELBASE!CreateProcessInternalW
KERNELBASE!CreateProcessW
KERNEL32!CreateProcessW
chrome.dll!uv_spawn
```

The child's image was git.exe from the installed Git for Windows distribution. Its working directory was the affected project repository. Paths, repository names, commit IDs, account details, and conversation content are intentionally omitted from this public report.

## Isolation results

- A clean restart verified zero ChatGPT/Codex processes before launching the desktop. It froze again within about 15 seconds, before another IDE/CLI Codex backend was present during the observation. Leftover backends do not explain this reproduction.
- Isolating the most recently used conversation and its seven child conversations did not fix the freeze.
- Restoring that conversation family while Git discovery remained paused succeeded: eight session files, 25 turns, and 1,303 history items were readable again. The restarted desktop window remained responsive.
- SQLite integrity checks and session JSON validation passed. This trigger does not require treating the history as corrupt.
- The relevant freeze observations had zero ResizeObserver-loop messages. Historical layout-loop warnings alone do not explain this captured native stall.

## Independent process-creation probes

Short read-only Git commands completed normally, including git --version and a one-file diff. Replaying the long diff in an independent PowerShell/.NET Process.Start probe also blocked inside process creation.

Additional padding probes on the same machine:

| Probe | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Git --version with padding targeting approximately 32,000 total characters | Completed normally |
| Git --version with padding targeting 32,500 total characters; actual total about 32,492 | Process creation blocked |
| Git --version with padding targeting 32,700 total characters; actual total about 32,692 | Process creation blocked |
| cmd.exe with padding targeting approximately 32,500 characters | Process creation blocked |

This points to a long-command process-creation problem on the affected Windows environment, not uniquely to Git. These values are observations, not a universal cutoff. No vendor/security product has been established as the cause.

### A short alternative was verified

A read-only metadata diff with the same baseline and diff flags, but without the individual path arguments, used a command line of approximately 352 characters. It completed in 2.93 seconds and returned 466 changed entries (112,741 output bytes). This demonstrates that this repository can be compared without constructing a 32K-character command. Integrating this alternative into the desktop would still require filtering the result to the requested paths and preserving the intended rename semantics; it has not been installed as a desktop patch.

Microsoft documents a maximum CreateProcessW command-line size of 32,767 characters, including the terminating null: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw

## Confirmed temporary workaround

Launch the desktop with a process-scoped GIT_DIR pointing to a deliberately nonexistent directory. Git then reports that the project is not a repository, and the automatic diff path is not reached.

This left the repositories and Windows global environment unchanged. After this launch, the main window remained responsive during two minutes of checks, and the user confirmed that project switching and opening conversations worked again. The conversation family was subsequently restored and the restarted window also stayed responsive.

This is a workaround: desktop Git functionality is unavailable, and child terminals/agent commands may inherit the GIT_DIR value. Removing GIT_DIR in a child shell allows normal Git use there. A regular launch without the workaround can retrigger the freeze.

## Bundled-code observation and possible fixes

Read-only inspection of this installed version's JavaScript bundle found the tracked review-summary command builder in .vite/build/worker.js. The minified function c4 constructs an argument array equivalent to:

```js
[...diffArgs, ...whitespaceOptions,
 '--find-renames', '--raw', '--no-abbrev', '--numstat', '-z',
 '--', ...paths]
```

That construction does not itself bound the accumulated path arguments. A separate untracked-file path already contains batching logic using a length budget and a file-count cap. A patch should audit both the summary path and other large multi-path diff calls, rather than assuming the untracked batching protects all Git launches.

Suggested maintainer fixes:

1. Bound the final Windows command length, accounting for executable name, flags, UTF-16 length, and Windows quoting/escaping. Use a generous margin below the OS maximum.
2. Avoid passing every changed path when a short whole-repository metadata diff followed by filtering is sufficient. Alternatively, batch paths while preserving correct rename detection and output semantics across boundaries. Do not assume git diff accepts the git add --pathspec-from-file flags.
3. Isolate native process creation in a separate utility/helper process so that a stuck CreateProcessW cannot block the main UI. A JavaScript timeout on the already blocked thread is insufficient.
4. Provide a supported option to pause automatic Git refresh while retaining normal project/chat use.

The installed app has not been patched. These are code-level findings and proposed fixes, not a claim that a permanent fix has been applied or that a specific driver is responsible.

## Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53697 describes an app-server-wide stall during an MCP server spawn. This report concerns the ChatGPT.exe window thread, automatic Git diff, and a long path-argument list, so the component and reproduction trigger differ. Both suggest that process-creation stalls should be isolated from critical threads; the precise underlying Windows cause is not assumed to be the same.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35776 describes a background Git loop and system resource exhaustion.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48666 describes accumulating Git processes and severe memory pressure.

They may share the automatic Git trigger, but this report adds a specifically captured long-command NtCreateUserProcess/uv_spawn stall with a process-scoped workaround. It is not claiming those reports have the identical root cause.

items.title: Android Remote saves phone-started threads under `openai`, then hides them when the host's default provider is custom

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex Desktop 26.1007.30912 (build 20156), bundled app-server 0.162.0-alpha.17.2. Phone: ChatGPT for Android, current release on 2026-10-13. The host logs the phone as `client_name="codex_chatgpt_android_remote"`, `client_version="dev"`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT (`planType: prolite`)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

On a host whose default provider is custom, every thread I start from ChatGPT Android Remote is saved under `openai`, but the phone's thread list only shows threads saved under the host's default provider. A thread started on the phone is visible while it runs, then drops out of the phone's list once it goes idle. Codex Desktop still lists it.

Host config, abbreviated:

```toml
model_provider = "custom"
openai_base_url = "<redacted>"   # the built-in openai provider is also routed, so both providers run turns normally

[model_providers.custom]
name = "Custom proxy"
base_url = "<redacted>"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
```

**Start and list disagree on the provider.** I matched every `thread/start` in the host log (`~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`) on 2026-10-13 to the row it created in `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`:

| Client that sent `thread/start` | Saved threads | Saved `model_provider` |
|---|---|---|
| `codex_chatgpt_android_remote` | 3 | `openai` (3 of 3) |
| `Codex Desktop` (user threads, automations, agent-created threads) | 9 | `custom` (9 of 9) |

The phone's list matches `thread/list` with `modelProviders` omitted, which the app-server resolves to the host default (#48358, #24648). Calling `thread/list` on the host with a `cwd` filter for one project:

| `modelProviders` | Threads returned |
|---|---|
| omitted | 2, both `custom`, the same 2 the phone shows |
| `[]` | 46 |
| `["openai"]` | 43 |

**What this looks like on the phone.** The newest thread in a project is often the missing one, because recent work started from the phone is saved under `openai`. Three projects on the same host:

- Project A shows its 2 `custom` threads. The other 44 are hidden, including one active the same evening as the visible ones.
- Project B hides its newest thread, which was started from the phone that afternoon, and shows 4 older `custom` threads.
- Project C shows the running thread plus 4 older `custom` threads, and hides two `openai` threads that were active earlier the same day. One of the two was started from the phone.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On a macOS host, set `model_provider` to a custom Responses provider (as above), stay signed in with ChatGPT, and enable Remote Control.
2. From ChatGPT for Android, open the host, start a new thread in any project, and let the turn finish.
3. On the host, check the saved provider: `sqlite3 ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite "select model_provider from threads order by created_at desc limit 1"` returns `openai`.
4. Close and reopen the thread list on the phone. The new thread is gone. Codex Desktop still shows it.
5. Optional: on the host, call `thread/list` with a `cwd` filter, once with `modelProviders` omitted and once with `modelProviders: []`. Only the second includes the phone-started thread.

### What is the expected behavior?

A thread started from the phone stays in the phone's list. Either change would do that:

- The Android Remote client sends `modelProviders: []` on `thread/list`, the spelling recommended in #48358, so the phone sees the same threads as Desktop.
- Remote `thread/start` saves the host's configured `model_provider`, so start and list agree.

The first also brings back Desktop threads that were saved under a non-default provider.

### Additional information

- **Thread cap and order within a project.** After the provider filter, the phone showed at most 4 idle threads per project, ordered by `updated_at` (last rollout write) instead of `recency_at` (last activity), which is how Desktop orders them. In two projects the phone's order matched `updated_at` descending exactly and the 5th thread was dropped. In one of them a thread sat at the top because its rollout file was written hours after its last turn, and in the other two threads appeared in the opposite order from their last activity. This pushes the most recently active thread out of view even among threads that pass the filter.
- **Related:** #24780 reports remote tasks disappearing on a custom-provider host where the phone-started task ran under the custom provider. Here the phone-started task is saved under `openai`, so the start/list mismatch hides it from the other direction. #48358 and #24648 cover the omitted-`modelProviders` default. #15494 covers provider switching hiding history. #22806 and #36454 cover project order on the phone.
- **Workarounds tried:** Switching the host default to `openai` only swaps which threads disappear. Rewriting the saved provider on existing threads would make the list complete but changes the provider used on resume, which #5658 was written to avoid.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Codex on native Windows can fan out one `git diff --binary --no-index` process per visible untracked path during `gitDiffToRemote`. Large local research/output trees turn this into a severe process and memory risk.

An independent local diagnostic established the per-file fan-out on a four-file disposable fixture. A custom mitigation subsequently added untracked files as intent-to-add entries. That avoided the per-file fan-out, but incorrectly included a large generated archive tree. This made full status checks extremely expensive. This report explicitly distinguishes the product behavior from that local mitigation mistake.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Business, x64, version 10.0.26200.
- Dell Precision 5690, approximately 32 GB installed RAM / 31.46 GiB usable.
- Desktop app checker: installedVersion 26.1007.21434, build 13901, prod.
- Current MSIX package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0. Package and app version identifiers are different.
- Bundled CLI checked on October 13: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Git for Windows 2.54.0.1.
- Native local workspace, not WSL. Mobile Remote is regularly used.
- Multiple concurrent tasks. No crash-inducing stress test was run.

## Directly verified observations

### 1. Per-file subprocess fan-out

A bounded, isolated four-untracked-file fixture was queried through the local app-server's `gitDiffToRemote`:

| Fixture | Per-file --no-index Git commands | Returned diff bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Four ordinary untracked text files | 4 | 608 |
| Same files registered as intent-to-add | 0 | 608 |

Before the local workaround, the affected real workspaces had 24,217 and 2,614 untracked paths respectively. Those counts are potential workload size; they are not claimed to be a simultaneous process census.

### 2. Very large resident memory in full Git status

On October 13 a live read-only command with this shape was recorded at **24.12 GiB working set**:

```text
git status --renames --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal
```

An earlier private-memory measurement for that process was approximately **0.207 GiB**. Resident memory and private commit are not interchangeable. Stopping that read-only status was followed by physical RAM utilization returning to approximately 45.3%.

### 3. Local workaround aggravated the status workload — corrected

Our custom normalizer had automatically registered roughly 70,700 files in a generated research/archive tree as intent-to-add. The tree had approximately 94.75 GiB **logical** file contents, including compressed/hardlinked historical copies. This is not 94.75 GiB newly created by Git, and is not its exclusive physical storage.

On October 13 at approximately 22:56 America/Toronto, we:
- added local exclusion rules for only these generated archive families;
- removed **70,708 intent-to-add entries** through a private-index transaction;
- verified every unrelated index entry and the prepared/staged raw diff were unchanged;
- left all working files untouched;
- prevented the normalizer from enrolling those archive families again.

The primary index went from **74,554 to 3,846 entries**. The same status command then completed successfully in **0.104 seconds**, with 19,417 output bytes and no stderr. The timing supports the generated-index workload as a major contributor on this machine. It does not prove that every historical failure had this cause.

### 4. Latest application closure was a custom safety action

October 13, America/Toronto (UTC-4):
- 22:17:13: Windows Application Error 1000 for git.exe, exception 0xc0000005.
- 22:18:16: a task started a broad shell Git status in the large primary workspace.
- 22:18:57: our independent guard recorded physical RAM at **95.98%**.
- 22:18:59: that guard intentionally closed the desktop/backends.
- 22:20:00: the guard reopened the desktop.
- The laptop's last boot remained 19:26:17; no laptop reboot occurred during this incident.

The latest desktop closure is therefore **not being reported as an unexplained native desktop crash**. The access violation, later shell status and missing historical resident-memory samples do not establish a complete causal chain. The guard originally covered GUI status but missed shell status; that gap has now also been corrected.

## Expected behavior / requested engineering changes

- Bound concurrent Git subprocesses globally and per repository in `gitDiffToRemote`, including the untracked-file path.
- Stream or cap path enumeration and diff output instead of eagerly scheduling a process for every untracked file.
- Coalesce repeated automatic scans and apply a circuit breaker/backoff after resource errors, cancellation or timeout.
- Correctly terminate and reap complete Git process trees on Windows.
- Allow supported disabling of expensive automatic Git review/status activity, including Remote-triggered work, without disabling agent execution or ordinary messages.
- Add diagnostics that distinguish resident mapped pages from private commit and identify the actual scan caller.
- Large generated research trees should cause a bounded unavailable/partial review result, never jeopardize the user's running tasks or OS.

## Related reports

- #41982: Remote chat opening and Windows Git/OOM incidents.
- #41091: composer_content/watch-repo full-status retries.
- #45172: Windows root-first cancellation race.
- #53645: thousands of app-server Git children in the current desktop build.

This report adds a bounded per-untracked-file reproduction, a directly observed 24.12 GiB status working set, and the measured effect of removing a mistakenly created bulk intent-to-add workload. It does not assert that all related reports share one proven root cause.

## Privacy

Text-only technical report. No raw logs, conversation exports, account identifiers, credentials, repository URLs, private project names, user-specific paths, or project contents are included.

Authentication complete. You may close this window.

However, the CLI exits with:
Error: failed to handle OAuth callback
Caused by:
OAuth token exchange failed: missing field `access_token` at line 1 column 191

A fresh configuration using automatic client registration fails with:
invalid_client_metadata: Dynamic registration is not available for this client.

RUST_LOG=debug and RUST_LOG=trace,codex_core=trace did not expose the token endpoint HTTP status or response body. Only the summarized error was captured.

Related report: #38944 describes a related Meta registration failure, but does not establish the cause of this token exchange error.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure https://mcp.facebook.com/ads as a Streamable HTTP MCP server, with a pre-registered OAuth client ID and the exact callback URI registered with the provider.

codex mcp login meta_ads

codex mcp add meta_ads_novo --url https://mcp.facebook.com/ads

This fails with:
invalid_client_metadata: Dynamic registration is not available for this client.

### What is the expected behavior?

With a valid pre-registered OAuth client and registered callback, Codex should complete the token exchange and save the credentials.

If the provider rejects the exchange, Codex should display the HTTP status and a sanitized provider error message, rather than only reporting a missing access_token field.

The callback page should distinguish receipt of the authorization code from successful completion of authentication.

### Additional information

The issue occurs during MCP authentication, before model usage.

Both the existing configuration with a pre-registered client and a fresh configuration using automatic registration were tested. They failed at different stages.

The underlying token endpoint response remains unknown, so the cause of the token exchange failure has not been established.

OpenAI support recommended filing this issue after debug and trace logging did not expose the original response. A redacted codex doctor report is included above.

No access tokens, client secrets, authorization codes, or full callback URLs are included in this report.

client_id: 1431989845511004

Codex CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
